title: Familiarity that hides someone’s worth
literal_meaning: The village bride is called runny-nosed.
explanation: People who have known someone from everyday village life may dismiss that person instead of recognizing their qualities. The belittling description makes that dismissiveness audible. The saying can challenge a narrow local judgment without endorsing the insult directed at the bride.
meaning_odia: ଅତି ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକର ଗୁଣ ଦେଖିବା ବଦଳରେ ତାଙ୍କ ପୁରୁଣା ବା ଛୋଟ ଦୋଷକୁ ମନେ ରଖାଯାଉଛି। ନିଜ ପାଖର ଲୋକକୁ ସହଜରେ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରିବାର ଅଭ୍ୟାସକୁ ଏହି କଥା ଧରେ। ବୋହୂଙ୍କ ପ୍ରତି ଥିବା ଅପମାନଜନକ ଉପମାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ ନକରି, ପରିଚୟ କିପରି ବିଚାରକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରେ ସେଥିରେ ମନ ଦିଆଯାଇପାରେ।
usage_example: A skilled local storyteller receives appreciation elsewhere while neighbours still speak only of childhood mistakes. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The literal image is gendered and dismissive. The editorial reading concerns undervaluing the familiar; neither a universal village custom nor the saying’s first historical use is known.
